notes.title: Lasts
notes.body:
As I get ready to depart, I find myself experiencing a multitude of lasts. For example, my mom and I went to our special park for lunch one last time, and I almost puked from swinging in the oppressing heat for so long. 

We also went to the waterpark that we went to every summer when I was little, and God was smiling down on us because, for the only time ever, the weather was perfect and there were zero lines! Plus, I was so brave; I did the two rides I chickened out of last time. Water went up every orifice, but I did it!

Finally, my dad and I went to Busch Gardens together for the last time. We stopped at the Candy Shoppe so I could get a big bag of sugar, just like my first trip to Busch Gardens, when I had scarlet fever, and my dad was sure a whole bunch of candy would set me straight.

I’ve still got a few more lasts before I leave to experience a whole bunch of firsts, and I’m trying to cherish every one of them. I’m going to miss this chapter of my life, but I know God has great big plans for me. Thanks for reading!

Love, Molly🌳

notes.title: She's Off.
notes.body: Molly left for Kona yesterday and arrived safely.  She arrived safely, was settling in, and headed to worship when Karen spoke to her last night.  Hawaii is six hours behind.  A hurricane is headed toward Hawaii, so the next couple of days should be interesting.  More to come....Molly's Dad.

notes.title: Big News!
notes.body:
Hi, everybody! I know I said I’d update every Saturday, and I’m so sorry I haven’t done that! I’ve been very busy… and I’m a huge procrastinator, but I’m working on it. I just wanted to go ahead and come on here and tell y’all something important. Today, we found out the options for our outreach locations! As soon as I heard them, one place was immediately on my heart. I heard God telling me over and over again, “Colombia, Colombia, Colombia, Colombia.” And I can’t see myself anywhere else for outreach. Of course, I prayed on it, but God only told me what I already knew. I did put the Philippines down as my second choice, but I’m trusting that the staff is praying and that God will tell them where I’m supposed to be. Anyways, I’ll work on updating more. But until then, send your spare change my way (if God leads you to), and pray for Colombia!

Love, Molly 🇨🇴

notes.title: OUTREACH REVEAL!!
notes.body:
Ladies and gentlemen, I am going to… 



🇨🇴 🇧🇷 🇵🇪 



COLOMBIA, BRAZIL, and PERU!!!



\
I don’t know how exactly it will go, or if I’ll even be able to post, but I’ll do my best! I will be spending Christmas doing kids ministry and then a month, including my birthday, in the Amazon Rainforest!! I’m gonna get eaten alive by skeeters, but I’m gonna be doing so much good work! I’m over the moon, I couldn’t have gotten a better team.

Got to go!

Love, Molly 📖

notes.title: Long Update pt. 1
notes.body:
Hey, y’all!

Sorry it’s been so long since I’ve last updated, but y’all know I struggle with that procrastination! Please, God, take it away!

So, since it’s been so long since I gave an update, I thought I’d just do one super long update going over all the major events and things that have happened since I got here. I’ll do my best to go in chronological order, but bear with me!

Ok, so I had a really hard time the first three days after arrival. I was homesick and lonely and just not sure how to connect with everyone and make new friends for the first time in years, because I got a touch of the ‘tism, as you may know. I reached my breaking point on that first Friday, when I was just so exhausted because I’d been pushing myself to make friends and just participate in everything, and I was just so overworked. But the Lord brought me to what has quickly become one of my favorite passages in the whole Bible, 1 Kings 19:4-8 which goes like this, “4 But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness and came and sat down under a broom tree. And he asked that he might die, saying, “It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life, for I am no better than my fathers.” \
“5 And he lay down and slept under a broom tree. And behold, an angel touched him and said to him, “Arise and eat.” \
“6 And he looked, and behold, there was at his head a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. And he ate and drank and lay down again. \
“7 And the angel of the LORD came again a second time and touched him and said, “Arise and eat, for the journey is too great for you.” \
“8 And he arose and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mount of God.”And I understood that He was telling me that I didn’t need to push myself so hard that I never rested. The journey would be too great for me if I did that. He built each one of us different and special, and He didn’t build me to be go, go, go all the time. I don’t need to participate in everything my roommates do, and I don’t need to have FOMO, because I am here for Him, not me. And if I just listen to Him, He’ll guide me in where to go and what to do. So I rested all day Saturday, and got up ready and energized for church on Sunday! \
Since then, listening to God, I’ve only been homesick one other time, on Halloween, when it truly sunk in that I wouldn’t get to do my Halloween traditions of dressing up, going trick-or-treating, and then watching the Halloween episodes of various sitcoms.

Ok, next big thing happened week two of lecture, Father Heart of God week. Y’all know me. Y’all know that I’m not exactly gifted in the athletic department. My own mother calls me Noodle Arms! But on Wednesday, we had our weekly DTS Olympics. That’s where the whole discipleship training school of 200+ college-aged kids participates in games of all sorts. I had a blast at the first one because it was not athletic, and my team won, so I was looking forward to the second night of Olympics, the one that this story is about. Until I arrived and found out we were playing DODGEBALL!! Big no-no for me. But I knew I had to participate. So I said a prayer that it would be quick and painless, and for my team to win. And the first round was quick and painless! I got hit in the ankle and quickly climbed over the barrier to the out part of the court. But the second round, I hid toward the very corner of the court, and stood so still and petrified that the opposing team didn’t even realize was playing until there was hardly anyone left. By then, there was just me and one other girl. The opposing team then noticed I was still in and started to target me. One of the people on the sidelines convinced me to pick up a ball and just hold it in front of me,  it even throw it. And thank goodness he did, because someone on the other team threw a ball that came right at my chest, and I blocked it with the ball in my hands! The other girl and I managed to stay in the game long enough for the timer to run out, securing our team the win! And even though the other girl was actually throwing balls and getting people out, I was so visibly petrified, physically shaking, that people seem to remember my performance far better than hers.

Ok, I’m going to have to make a part two because my iPad is about to die, and I need to publish what I’ve written so far before it does.

TTYL, 

Molly 🏐

notes.title: Long Update pt. 2
notes.body:
Ok, I’m back for the second half of my long update.

So, the next day, after Olympics, was the final day of the week of Father Heart of God. I was really struggling to connect to the lecturer. The week before had been just so amazing, and the lecturer was so funny, and Holy Spirit just really spoke through him. The Father Heart of God lecturer just didn’t teach in a style that I learn in, plus he said some things I really didn’t agree with. But on the last day, he had printed out over 200 copies of the https://www.fathersloveletter.com/text.html so every one of us got a copy. And I didn’t have high expectations, but as I’m reading it, God’s just moving in my heart, and I’m in tears. And I was embarrassed, because I was in a class of roughly 230 people and I’m sobbing in front of all of them. And the lecturer started praying for me by name, and even commended my pathetic volleyball performance. It was then that I realized that, up until that point, I’d been viewing God as The Father, not my Father. I ended up realizing that I needed to go back to therapy, and they offer that at YWAM. I did one hour long session of their 9941 counseling, and I’m fully committing, telling the counselor lady about all my trauma, and, like, less than fifteen minutes in, she’s like, “I think an RTF would be really helpful for you.” An RTF is a Restoring The Foundations therapy. It’s basically where you heal non-biblical beliefs. And so I did that, too, and it really healed something in me. And now I’m, like, recommending it to everyone who tells me about their issues.

Ok, I really don’t have anything else big to tell y’all, except that I’m trying to get over a crush I have on a guy here. I don’t want to say too much about him on this, in case he somehow comes across this, but text me, and I’ll tell you as much as you want to know.

Also, I leave for Colombia on December 12th. I’m super excited, but I still have to pay for the flights, which is an additional $2175 that I do not have. So please, pray about it and, if you are called, send me your spare change, or whatever God calls you to give.

Lastly, I’d love to talk with anyone who wishes to speak with me. So, email me or ask one of my parents, and we’ll send you my number. Also, I thought I’d include my mailing address for anyone who wants to send me a physical letter or something (as long as it gets here before December 12th)

Molly Measells

Kona DTS, Q4 2026

U of N, Kona

75-5851 Kuakini Hwy, Box #250

Kailua-Kona, HI 96740 



OK, love y’all! Talk soon!

Lots of Love,

Molly ✝️
